fullPassage: In the United States, the practice of permitting aliens to vote could be seen as compatible with the idea of an exclusionary citizenship, but that is a hard balance to maintain. If the vote, of all rights, is in the hands of noncitizens, why should they not count as citizens, and the entire distinction between resident alien and citizen be abandoned? Indeed, something like this thought probably lay behind the disappearance of alien voting: with universal adult citizen suffrage after 1920, the only way to maintain an exclusionary kind of citizenship was to restrict the vote to citizens and not residents. But no theory of "active" democracy can countenance this distinction: the laws concerning our common life must be made by all those who are taking part in it, and residence is the only convincing test of whether someone is taking part — as is understood almost universally when it comes to questions of which citizens should have a voice in local government.

det.tip: exclude(배제하다/동사) → exclusion(배제/명사) → exclusionary(배타적인/형용사)

questions.passage: But no theory of "active" democracy can countenance this distinction: the laws concerning our common life must be made by all those who are taking part in it, and (reside) is the only convincing test of whether someone is taking part.
questions.stem: 다음 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 변형하시오.

det.korean: 거주(residence)가 유일한 설득력 있는 기준이다.
det.analysis: reside(동사) → residence(명사): 주어 자리에 명사 필요
det.tip: reside(거주하다/동사) → residence(거주/명사) → resident(거주자/명사)

questions.passage: In the United States, the practice of permitting aliens to vote could be seen as compatible with the idea of an exclusionary citizenship, but that is a hard balance to maintain. If the vote, of all rights, is in the hands of noncitizens, why should they not count as citizens, and the entire distinction between resident alien and citizen be abandoned? Indeed, something like this thought probably lay behind the disappearance of alien voting: with universal adult citizen suffrage after 1920, the only way to maintain an exclusionary kind of citizenship was to restrict the vote to citizens and not residents. But no theory of "active" democracy can countenance this distinction: the laws concerning our common life must be made by all those who are taking part in it, and __________ is the only convincing test of whether someone is taking part — as is understood almost universally when it comes to questions of which citizens should have a voice in local government.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 거주(residence)가 누군가 참여하고 있는지의 유일한 설득력 있는 기준이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② residence: 거주, 원문 일치 — 공동체 참여의 기준
❌ ① nationality: 국적, 본문의 논지와 반대
❌ ③ profession: 직업, 무관
❌ ④ ethnicity: 민족성, 무관
det.tip: residence(거주) — 글의 핵심 논지: 거주가 민주적 참여의 유일한 기준

det.korean: 공동 생활에 관한 법률은 그것에 참여하고 있는 모든 사람들에 의해 만들어져야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ all those who are taking part in it: 원문 일치
❌ ① elected representatives only: 선출된 대표만, 본문 논지와 불일치
❌ ② citizens with legal status: 법적 지위 시민, 배타적 시민권 논지
❌ ③ those who pay taxes: 납세자, 본문에 언급 없음
det.tip: all those who are taking part — '능동적 민주주의'의 핵심: 참여하는 모든 사람이 법 제정에 참여
